messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: GPU pool 'prod-gpu-a' queue_growth > 90% for 6m. Severity: P1. @carla_oncall you are on rotation. Paging details: https://pager.example/incident/2165409876 :rotating_light:
carla_oncall: seeing huge enqueue on request-queue, tail latency spiking. Autoscaler keeps failing to add nodes, eviction/throttle rising to 40%. Investigating.
alice_sre: looking at cluster events — lots of 'driver crash' on nodes n-gpu-04..n-gpu-07. kubectl logs show repeated CUDA Xid 13 errors.
ben_runtime: past 3 hours we had intermittent kernel OOMs on those nodes; quality of service dropped. Hypothesis: driver + runtime combo causing GPU devices to become unusable -> autoscaler thinks nodes healthy but cannot run pods.
frank_infra: autoscaler logs: scale-up attempts hit GCE quota limit for the region, causing backoff. Also saw kubelet reporting 'device plugin lost' on the same hosts.
evelyn_support: Customer-facing impact: embded/real-time customers on prod-gpu-a seeing 5-12s stallouts and some 500s. I'm drafting status for customers — any ETA? We need mitigation ASAP. :warning:
dave_pm: priority is to restore capacity. Can we shift traffic to fallback pools or degrade to smaller model?
carla_oncall: immediate plan: 1) cordon n-gpu-04..n-gpu-07 2) drain gracefully (preStop 30s) 3) restart driver on those hosts 4) force fallback routing for high-latency routes to smaller model. Starting step 1 now.
alice_sre: sharing commands I'm running:
```kubectl cordon n-gpu-04
kubectl drain n-gpu-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
ssh root@n-gpu-04 'systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service || journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200'```
ben_runtime: logs from n-gpu-05 dmesg (snippet):
```[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, pid=22401, Graphics Exception: EE %llx
[  123.456800] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.```
This matches previous OOM/Xid waves from driver 460.x; we rolled a compat change last week.
frank_infra: GCE quota cannot be bumped quickly; I've requested emergency quota from cloud-ops but likely 30+ mins. Will attempt to bring back existing nodes by restarting drivers.
evelyn_support: notifying top 5 customers now with a note that we're experiencing GPU capacity issues; offering SLA temporarily and workaround (use batch endpoints).
dave_pm: good. Also flip routing for non-critical traffic to 'prod-gpu-b' (lower-cost pool) until stabilized. Who can update routing?
carla_oncall: @ben_runtime will apply a routing rule to prioritize latency-sensitive requests to prod-gpu-b if model fits. Ben?
ben_runtime: on it — adding temporary traffic-split: 70% -> prod-gpu-b, 30% stay (to reduce overload), will enable model quantization fallback for the split. Pushing change in 2m.
carla_oncall: driver restarts in progress on n-gpu-04..n-gpu-07. Observed node-level device plugin come back on n-gpu-04 after restart. Monitoring queue.
incident-bot: autoscaler: scale_up_attempt failed (quota_exceeded) at 2165409898.
alice_sre: after restarts, nvidia-smi on n-gpu-04 shows all GPUs present. Running a smoke job now.
ben_runtime: smoke job passed on n-gpu-04. Queue decreased 18% after routing change and drains. Tail latency trending down.
frank_infra: autoscaler still hitting quota for new nodes; cloud-ops responded, exp turning at 20-30m. We'll keep the workaround.
evelyn_support: updated customers with mitigation note + request to use alternate endpoints. No escalations yet.
dave_pm: ok, once queue below 30% and tail latency < 200ms for 10m, we'll start lifting restrictions. Keep me posted.
carla_oncall: will leave thread open for handoff. @alice_sre you take next on-call in 35 mins? please monitor queue and driver's stability.
alice_sre: taking handoff. I'll watch for Xid reoccurrence and autoscaler logs. Leaving note: possible regression from last driver shim; file a postmortem if this repeats.
carla_oncall: thanks. Marking incident as 'mitigating' — next update in 15m. :white_check_mark:
